title: How to Become a UGC Content Creator
summary: Learn how to build a UGC portfolio, define usage terms, approach brands, disclose partnerships, and manage creator projects professionally.
body_markdown:
## Set terms and find legitimate work


### Build a quote from the scope


Rates vary too widely for a universal promise. Quote from the number and complexity of assets, research, scripting, filming, editing, revision rounds, turnaround, raw files, usage channels, duration, paid advertising, and exclusivity. Separate production from licensing so both sides understand what is included.


### Use a written agreement


Record deliverables, due dates, review process, revision limit, payment schedule, cancellation, product handling, claims approval, usage rights, credit, and confidentiality. Clarify whether you or the brand publishes the work. Keep invoices and approvals with the project files.


### Vet opportunities before starting


Confirm the company, contact domain, product, brief, contract, and payment process. Treat requests for upfront fees, gift-card purchases, account credentials, unexplained overpayments, or off-platform transfers as warning signs. Never give a client login access to your social accounts.


### Pitch with a relevant idea


A concise pitch should identify a real product fit, propose one or two specific concepts, link to the most relevant examples, and ask about the brand's current brief. Avoid mass claims about guaranteed performance. Follow up once or twice professionally and track replies.
